# `dec.pdf()` {#fn-dec-pdf}

**Verified on 2.0.9006.** Declination subsets retained the selected centres in all four cases. [D01 rerun](d01-density-checks.qmd).

**Validation on 2.0.9005.** The sampled declination densities agreed with analytic references at the tested bounds and cutoffs. Subsetting curves can leave stale input centres in metadata$dec. [D01 results](d01-density-checks.qmd).

[Function index](function-index.html#idx-dec-pdf)

```{=html}
<p>Use this constructor when both the measurement and its uncertainty
are already expressed in declination. All six families have the same parameter
meaning as in <code>az.pdf</code>. The doorway examples in 'Choosing a
measurement model' illustrate their shapes. When starting from measured bearings
and site horizons, use <code>coordtrans</code> to propagate the bearing model.
Direct declinations are linear. A triangle must satisfy lower &lt;= dec &lt;= upper.
The sampled curve is clipped to physical declinations from -90 to +90 degrees
and trimmed at <code>.cutoff</code>. The retained area can consequently be less than one.
</p>
```

[Field examples and comparison of all six profiles](orientation-densities.qmd#measurement-families).
